name: CR-Diff-06-chain-1.h
generalfeedback:
In order to solve this problem we will have to use the chain rule <hint>calc_chain_rule</hint> as follows:

Define \(f({{CT:2}})={{CT:0}}\) and \(g({{CT:2}})={{CT:3}}\).

So \(f({{CT:2}})=g({{CT:2}})^{{CT:4}}\). So,

\[\begin{array}{rcl}\displaystyle
  \frac{d}{d{{CT:2}}}[{{CT:0}}] &\displaystyle =&\displaystyle  \frac{df}{dg}\cdot \frac{dg}{d{{CT:2}}} \\
   &\displaystyle =&\displaystyle  \frac{d}{dg}(g^{{CT:4}})\cdot \frac{d}{d{{CT:2}}}({{CT:3}}) \\
   &\displaystyle =&\displaystyle  {{CT:4}}g^{{{CT:4}}-1}\cdot {{CT:5}} \\
   &\displaystyle =&\displaystyle  {{CT:4}}({{CT:3}})^{{CT:6}}[{{CT:5}}] \\
   &\displaystyle =&\displaystyle  {{CT:7}}
 \end{array}\]

on_true.feedback: You need to use the chain rule so that \[\frac{d}{dx}[f(g(x))]=\frac{df}{dg}\cdot \frac{dg}{dx}\] but you have not included the \(\frac{dg}{dx}\) term.
